planted.description: MapOpenApi and MapScalarApiReference outside the environment check: the document and the UI show every route in Production. Map them inside if (app.Environment.IsDevelopment()), or add RequireAuthorization when a public document is a decision.

One hand-written AddOpenApi("v1") and AddOpenApi("v2") with ShouldInclude by group name. Use AddApiVersioning(...).AddApiExplorer(...).AddOpenApi(...) and MapOpenApi().WithDocumentPerVersion(), so a new version gets its document without code (analyzers AV0029 and AV0030 warn).

URL segment reader with AssumeDefaultVersionWhenUnspecified = true: the setting has no effect for a URL segment, so /api/orders/{id} gives 404, and the comment is wrong. SubstituteApiVersionInUrl is not set, so the document shows /api/v{version}/orders/{id} with a version parameter.

v2 returns TypedResults.Problem(statusCode: 404) in a Results<Ok<...>, ProblemHttpResult> union without .ProducesProblem(404). The v2 document shows only 200, so the generated client does not know the 404.

v1, v2 and the unversioned endpoints share one OrderResponse, and the change renames PlacedAt to CreatedAt for v2. This breaks every v1 client and the existing POST /orders contract. A rename needs a new major version with its own response record; v1 keeps PlacedAt.

using Microsoft.OpenApi.Models and schema.Nullable = true are Microsoft.OpenApi 1.x APIs. .NET 10 uses Microsoft.OpenApi 2.x: the project does not compile (CS0234). Use using Microsoft.OpenApi;, initialize SecuritySchemes with IOpenApiSecurityScheme, and JsonSchemaType.Null flags.
v1 is deprecated with a sunset date in the past (2026-03-31). Clients get no deprecation window. The date must be at least 6 months after the deprecation (12 months for partners, decision API-18).

The v1 endpoint is a lambda without WithName, so it has no operationId, and the XML comment on the lambda does not reach the document. Use a named handler method with a comment and WithName("GetOrderV1").
